hints: Set the proportionality relation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = k x(300 - x)$ where $k$ is a constant.
Substitute the initial values $x = 1$ and $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0.2$ at $t = 0$ to solve for $k = \dfrac{1}{1495}$.
walkthrough:
Write the differential equation representing the rate of infection:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \propto x(300 - x) \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = k x(300 - x)$$
where $k$ is a positive constant of proportionality.

Substitute the initial condition $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0.2$ when $x = 1$ at $t = 0$:
$$0.2 = k(1)(300 - 1)$$
$$0.2 = 299k$$

Solve for the constant $k$ as an exact fraction:
$$k = \dfrac{0.2}{299} = \dfrac{2}{2990} = \dfrac{1}{1495}$$

Substitute $k = \dfrac{1}{1495}$ into the rate equation:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{x(300 - x)}{1495}$$

Multiply through by $1495$ to obtain the required differential equation:
$$1495\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = x(300 - x)$$

ai_rubric.Differential-Equation Modelling: States or implies $dx/dt = kx(300 - x)$ and uses initial condition to find $k = 1/1495$ (M1). Rearranges to $1495(dx/dt) = x(300 - x)$ (A1).

skill_tags: Applying Initial Conditions to Differential Equations

hints: Use partial fractions: $\dfrac{1}{x(300 - x)} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{300 - x}$ to find $A = B = \dfrac{1}{300}$.
Integrate both sides and substitute the initial condition $t = 0, x = 1$ to find the constant.
Use the laws of logarithms to combine terms into an expression for $t$ involving a single logarithm.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation $1495\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = x(300 - x)$:
$$\dfrac{1495}{x(300 - x)}\,\mathrm{d}x = \mathrm{d}t$$
$$\int \dfrac{1495}{x(300 - x)}\,\mathrm{d}x = \int 1\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate the right-hand side with respect to $t$:
$$\int 1\,\mathrm{d}t = t + C$$

Decompose $\dfrac{1}{x(300 - x)}$ into partial fractions:
$$\dfrac{1}{x(300 - x)} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{300 - x}$$
$$1 = A(300 - x) + Bx$$
- Setting $x = 0 \implies 300A = 1 \implies A = \dfrac{1}{300}$
- Setting $x = 300 \implies 300B = 1 \implies B = \dfrac{1}{300}$

Multiply by $1495$:
$$\dfrac{1495}{x(300 - x)} = \dfrac{1495}{300}\left( \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{300 - x} \right)$$
Simplify the fraction $\dfrac{1495}{300}$ by dividing numerator and denominator by $5$:
$$\dfrac{1495 \div 5}{300 \div 5} = \dfrac{299}{60}$$
So:
$$\dfrac{1495}{x(300 - x)} = \dfrac{299}{60}\left( \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{300 - x} \right)$$

Integrate the left-hand side with respect to $x$:
$$\int \dfrac{299}{60}\left( \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{300 - x} \right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{299}{60}\left( \ln x - \ln(300 - x) \right)$$

Equate the integrated expressions:
$$\dfrac{299}{60}\left( \ln x - \ln(300 - x) \right) = t + C$$
$$\dfrac{299}{60}\ln\left( \dfrac{x}{300 - x} \right) = t + C$$

Substitute the initial condition $t = 0$ when $x = 1$ to evaluate $C$:
$$\dfrac{299}{60}\ln\left( \dfrac{1}{300 - 1} \right) = 0 + C$$
$$C = \dfrac{299}{60}\ln\left( \dfrac{1}{299} \right) = -\dfrac{299}{60}\ln(299)$$

Substitute $C$ back into the solution:
$$\dfrac{299}{60}\ln\left( \dfrac{x}{300 - x} \right) = t - \dfrac{299}{60}\ln(299)$$

Isolate $t$ and combine the terms using logarithm laws:
$$t = \dfrac{299}{60}\ln\left( \dfrac{x}{300 - x} \right) + \dfrac{299}{60}\ln(299)$$
$$t = \dfrac{299}{60}\left[ \ln\left( \dfrac{x}{300 - x} \right) + \ln(299) \right]$$
$$t = \dfrac{299}{60}\ln\left( \dfrac{299x}{300 - x} \right)$$

ai_rubric.Applying Initial Conditions to Different: Separates variables correctly (B1). Integrates $t$ term correctly (B1). States partial fractions $A/x + B/(300-x)$ and obtains $A = B = 1/300$ (B1M1). Integrates to $\frac{299}{60}(\ln x - \ln(300-x))$ (A1). Evaluates constant using $t=0, x=1$ (M1A1). Uses log laws to obtain $t = \frac{299}{60}\ln[299x/(300-x)]$ in terms of a single logarithm (M1A1).
